name: TensorFlow
what_it_is: An end-to-end platform for machine learning, per its own documentation, operating on multidimensional arrays called tensors. Beyond the library it covers the surrounding steps — export, serving and on-device runtimes — under one project.
why_it_matters: Its reach past training is the reason to know it: the export and serving path is part of the project rather than something assembled afterwards, and mobile and browser runtimes are first-party. The trade-off is a larger surface to learn, much of which is irrelevant if you only ever train.
suitable_for: Work where serving and on-device deployment are in scope from the start
Codebases already built on it, where the migration cost is real
Teams who want export and serving from one project
not_suitable_for: Reproducing research published against another framework
Small experiments, where the platform surface exceeds the problem
Teams who only train and never deploy, who pay for reach they do not use
